goal: Can TRACE preserve a complete, replayable record of a lived experience in real time, then answer truthfully across TWO different videos without leaked facts or entity mix-ups? Capture gets exactly the clip duration; post-capture reasoning may take as long as needed.
headline_metric: Two numbers, in plain English: (1) How many of the 25 questions it gets RIGHT, and (2) how often it CONFIDENTLY MAKES SOMETHING UP (a hallucination). A wrong, confident answer is the worst outcome; an honest 'I don't know' is a WIN, not a loss. The score 'RAS' = (right − made-up) out of 25. Goal: made-up → ZERO, right → as high as honestly possible.
why_two_bars: For 10 days a single bar sat at 25% and looked stuck. That bar measured the FULL wearable product (always-on capture, on-device, the nightly sleep loop, sensors) — a much bigger, later build. It was honest but it measured the wrong thing for right now. The CHIEF's actual current mission is the PROOF above, and that IS moving. So the cockpit now tracks the proof mission. The full-wearable bar is parked until the proof lands.
progress_basis: Acceptance gates, not elapsed effort: clip isolation 1/1; honest two-video baseline 1/1; tail-complete derived capture 1/1; tested entity ownership 1/1; mandatory raw A/V evidence pack 0/1; zero-gap replay ledger 0/1; query-time raw-evidence replay 0/1; >=50% correct on both clips 0/1; <15% hallucination on both clips 0/1; fresh independent critics pass both clips 0/1. Four of ten gates pass, so 40% is the defensible number.
quality_state: HONEST BASELINE, NOT RESPECTABLE YET — COLD 6/19 right and 40% hallucination; WALK 10/25 right and 41.2% hallucination

milestones.name: Phase 0 — Honest baseline + a truth-detector on every answer
milestones.note: Frozen 25-question answer key from YOUR ground truth. Every answer now logs WHAT the brain looked at, so a miss is diagnosed: (A) we never captured it, or (B) we captured it but the brain mis-used it. Honest floor reproduced: RAS -4 / 54% made-up.

milestones.name: Phase 1 — Capture everything cheaply; answer the spatial 'which side' questions
milestones.note: Win tonight: 'which side is Max-Planck / the lift' now answered from the camera's own panning motion (no extra sensor) — left & right both correct, with proof. Full version (real compass + GPS) waits on a re-recording with the sensor app.

milestones.name: Phase 2 — Close capture-gaps + drive MADE-UP answers toward zero
milestones.note: Tonight: built the two memory channels the brain was blind to — READING THE LAPTOP SCREEN (found the chat asking for input + the unsent draft) and the NIGHTLY BINDING pass (counted the posters, tied each scientist to the right poster). Fixed a real bug: the brain's reading-window was too small and was cutting answers off mid-word. Now re-scoring.

milestones.name: Phase 3 — Where the fact was captured but mis-used, fix the brain's wiring
milestones.note: Found the safety-check was wrongly DELETING some correct answers (e.g. the poster years) to be safe. Tightened it so it still catches genuine mix-ups but stops killing right answers. Re-scoring now.

milestones.name: Phase 4 — Prove it generalizes: a COLD second clip it has never seen
milestones.note: ACTIVE ROOT-FIX SPRINT. Found cross-clip contamination: the day memory contained the walk's hard-coded Garching/poster bindings. Added source fingerprints, rebuilt both clips independently, completed entity capture + re-ID on the day, and now applying the identical capture path to the walk before rescoring all 44 questions. No headline win will be accepted from one clip alone.

milestones.name: Phase 5 — Package the pitch: the demo + the 'we literally can't spy on you' proof
milestones.note: Frames turn to text and get deleted on screen; the store is shown text-only. Plus a one-slide market beat. Rehearsed end-to-end so you can run it without me in the room.

milestones.name: THE GOAL — a stranger asks about your day and is amazed, and it never lies

walls_hit.wall: Adding the new memory channels SILENTLY REGRESSED the score — answers were truncating mid-word ('Wil', 'The'). It looked like the channels hurt; really the brain's context window was too small for the richer memory.
walls_hit.reroute: Diagnosed it as an infrastructure limit (not a channel problem), raised the window, verified answers are full again. This is the (A)/(B) discipline working: measure, find the real cause, fix THAT.

walls_hit.wall: Risk of tunnel vision: grinding one 25-question clip can produce a number that looks good but doesn't generalize.
walls_hit.reroute: Stood up an INDEPENDENT critic (a separate set of reviewers that reads the raw files, not my summary, and cannot be spun by me) to judge honestly whether we're really progressing. Its verdict shows in this cockpit.
